samples.summary: Toolbar Undo/Redo bypass the new "mutation clears the image selection" invariant. `undoFn` (editor.ts:2090) and `redoFn` (editor.ts:2122) call `docStore.undo()` + `doc.refresh()` and never touch `selectedImage`. The keyboard path is safe only by accident — ⌘Z reaches `imageKeyHandler`'s catch-all, which clears the selection — but the toolbar buttons call `EditorAPI.undo()/redo()` directly and skip it entirely. After a toolbar undo that shifts offsets, `selectedImage` names whatever inline slid into that slot; the new `imageSelectionProvider` only re-validates that *an* image is at the offset, so ⌘C copies the wrong image and cut/Delete (`deleteSelectedImageInline`) removes the wrong image. `render()` (editor.ts:1900) will also draw the selection overlay around it.
samples.evidence: packages/frontend/src/app/docs/docs-formatting-toolbar.tsx:272 `const handleUndo = useCallback(() => editor?.undo(), [editor]);` (and :273 for redo) — reaches editor.ts:2090/2122, neither of which calls `clearImageSelectionForMutation()`. Fix belongs in the new code: add the clear to `undoFn`/`redoFn`.

samples.summary: `resetAfterDocumentReplace` replaces the entire document (import / "replace content") and clears `pending`, the cursor and the text selection, but not `selectedImage`. It is another mutation entry point outside the funnel the diff created. Afterwards the selection names a block id that no longer exists in the new document: `getSelectedImage()`/`updateSelectedImage()` then call the throwing `doc.getBlock` (editor.ts:3780, 3793), and if a block id happens to collide the selection names an unrelated inline that cut/Delete would remove.
samples.evidence: packages/frontend/src/app/docs/docs-view.tsx:360 `editor.resetAfterDocumentReplace();` — the whole-document replace path; editor.ts:3874-3886 clears cursor/selection/layout cache but leaves `selectedImage` set. Fix belongs in the new code (`resetAfterDocumentReplace` should call `clearImageSelectionForMutation()`).

samples.summary: The diff hardened the *new* stale-selection readers (`imageSelectionProvider` uses `doc.findBlock`, `deleteSelectedImageInline` re-validates) but left the two pre-existing public readers of the same state on the throwing `doc.getBlock`. `getSelectedImage()` (editor.ts:3780) and `updateSelectedImage()` (editor.ts:3793) now sit behind a selection that is easier than before to leave stale (a read-only viewer can create one; remote refresh, toolbar undo and document replace all leave it), so a caller of either API can take a thrown exception where the sibling path silently returns null. Out of step with the contract the rest of the change adopts.
samples.evidence: packages/docs/src/view/editor.ts:3780 `const block = doc.getBlock(selectedImage.blockId);` vs the new packages/docs/src/view/editor.ts:2320 `const block = doc.findBlock(selectedImage.blockId);`. No in-repo production caller of `getSelectedImage`/`updateSelectedImage` exists today (only packages/docs/test/view/copy-integrity.test.ts), which is why this is minor.

samples.summary: The rewritten `getSelectedBlocks()` resolves cell parentage through `this.getLayout().blockParentMap`, but every context-aware sibling in the same class uses `this.getActiveLayout()` — including `isInTable()` (text-editor.ts:3403), which is what the frontend context menus branch on. `getLayout()` is the body layout, so a copy/cut inside a *header or footer* table cell still falls through to the body block list, finds nothing, and emits an empty rich payload — the exact #872 symptom the change is fixing for body tables. The repo already records this trap: docs/design/docs/docs-font-controls.md:513-516 says parentage must come from the merged map, "not the body-only `layout.blockParentMap`".
samples.evidence: packages/docs/src/view/text-editor.ts:3403 `return this.getActiveLayout().blockParentMap.has(blockId);` (isInTable) vs the new text-editor.ts:3794 `const cellInfo = layout.blockParentMap.get(start.blockId);` where `layout = this.getLayout()`.

samples.summary: The context menu's Copy gate is `hasSelection = !!editor.getActiveSelection()`, and `getActiveSelection()` returns null unless there is a non-collapsed *text* range (editor.ts:3311-3319) — `selectImageInline` explicitly does `selection.setRange(null)`. So a click-selected image produces no Copy entry (in read-only the menu does not open at all), contradicting the justification repeated throughout the new editor.ts comments ("which is exactly where the context menu now offers Copy", editor.ts:1253, 2553). The image copy the change adds is keyboard-only; the menu was not taught about image selection.
samples.evidence: packages/frontend/src/app/docs/docs-context-menu.tsx:74 `const hasSelection = !!editor.getActiveSelection();` against packages/docs/src/view/editor.ts:3311-3319 (returns null for a collapsed/absent range) and editor.ts:1255 `selection.setRange(null)` in `selectImageInline`.

verdict.reason: Verified in-repo. `clearImageSelectionForMutation` (editor.ts:1282) documents the invariant that every offset-shifting mutation clears `selectedImage`, but `undoFn` (editor.ts:2090-2120) and `redoFn` (editor.ts:2122-2152) mutate the doc via `docStore.undo()/redo()` + `doc.refresh()` and never clear it — they only reset cursor and text selection. They are exported as `undo`/`redo` at editor.ts:3015-3016, and the toolbar calls them directly at packages/frontend/src/app/docs/docs-formatting-toolbar.tsx:272-273 (buttons at :614/:623), bypassing `imageKeyHandler`, whose catch-all at editor.ts:2426 is what makes the keyboard ⌘Z path safe. No other guard covers it: `handleBlur` (editor.ts:2857) does not clear the selection, the container mousedown clear (editor.ts:2627) only fires for clicks inside the editor, and the read-only neutralisation (editor.ts:3939-3950) only applies when readOnly. Re-validation is insufficient: `imageSelectionProvider` (editor.ts:2320-2324) and `deleteSelectedImageInline` (editor.ts:2297-2302) only check that *an* image sits at the offset, so a different image that slid into the slot is copied or deleted, and render() (editor.ts:1900-1902) paints the overlay around it. This is a genuine blast-radius finding: an invariant introduced in the diff with a reachable bypass at a call site outside it.

finding.summary: Removing the `readOnly` early return from `handleImageMouseDown` makes the capture-phase handler swallow image mousedowns in view-only mode, so TextEditor's read-only link-follow path never records the href — a hyperlinked image that used to open its link on click in a shared/viewer document now does nothing.
finding.evidence: packages/docs/src/view/text-editor.ts:1667 `if (this.readOnly) { this.readOnlyPendingLinkHref = this.getLinkHrefAtMouse(e) ?? null; }` and the mouseup that consumes it at text-editor.ts:1991 only run if TextEditor's bubble-phase mousedown listener is reached. editor.ts:2586-2595 now calls `e.stopPropagation(); e.stopImmediatePropagation();` on any image-body hit in read-only too (the `if (readOnly) return;` at the top of `handleImageMouseDown` was deleted), so a click on an image inline carrying a link style never sets `readOnlyPendingLinkHref`. The same blockage also removes the ability to start a read-only drag-selection on top of an image.

verdict.reason: The finding's core assertion — that a read-only click on a hyperlinked image "never sets readOnlyPendingLinkHref" because the capture handler stops propagation — is false in this repository. editor.ts:2614 calls `textEditorRef?.recordReadOnlyLinkAtMouse(e)` immediately before `e.stopPropagation(); e.stopImmediatePropagation();` (editor.ts:2615-2616), and text-editor.ts:1637-1640 sets `this.readOnlyPendingLinkHref = this.getLinkHrefAtMouse(e) ?? null` when read-only. The consuming mouseup is a separate listener (`container.addEventListener('mouseup', this.handleMouseUp)`, text-editor.ts:579), so stopping the mousedown does not suppress it; handleMouseUp at text-editor.ts:2005-2016 then opens the href. The collapsed precondition holds because selectImageInline calls `selection.setRange(null)` (editor.ts:1256), making `range` null → collapsed. `getLinkHrefAtMouse` (text-editor.ts:5579-5603) reads `inline.style.href` at the hit offset, covering an image inline with a link style. The reviewer also mis-cited the assignment location (claimed 1667; actually 1639, inside the new public arming method rather than handleMouseDown). The secondary aside about read-only drag-selection over an image is a deliberate behaviour of the diff's own new code (documented at editor.ts:2546-2557) and is a correctness/design-fit judgement of the diff, not a broken or bypassing call site outside it.

finding.summary: The new "every mutation that shifts offsets clears the image selection" invariant has entry points outside `editor.ts` that bypass `clearImageSelectionForMutation()` — most concretely `FindReplaceState`, which the frontend drives directly against the Doc.
finding.evidence: packages/frontend/src/app/docs/docs-find-bar.tsx:118 `state.replaceActive(replacement);` and :126 `state.replaceAll(replacement);` call into packages/docs/src/view/find-replace.ts:61/69 → `replaceMatch` (find-replace.ts:78), which deletes+inserts text of a different length and shifts every following offset. Nothing on that path routes through `clearImageSelectionForMutation` (editor.ts:1275), so a click-selected image's `(blockId, offset)` can end up naming a different image inline — and `imageSelectionProvider` (editor.ts:2307) only re-validates that *an* image sits at the offset, so a subsequent Cmd+X copies and deletes the wrong picture. `undoFn`/`redoFn` (editor.ts:2083, 2115) and the table row/column ops (editor.ts:3578-3627) are further unguarded entry points of the same shape.

verdict.reason: The claimed bypass does not exist: the find bar explicitly clears the image selection before both replace paths. `handleReplace` calls `editor?.clearImageSelection()` at docs-find-bar.tsx:124 immediately before `state.replaceActive(replacement)` at :125, and `handleReplaceAll` calls it at :133 before `state.replaceAll(replacement)` at :134. That exported API member is bound directly to the helper the finding says is bypassed — `clearImageSelection: clearImageSelectionForMutation` at editor.ts:3777, helper defined at editor.ts:1282 — and the helper's own doc comment at editor.ts:1276-1280 documents this find-bar seam as the deliberate out-of-module path. The optional chain is not a hole: the effect at docs-find-bar.tsx:49-58 nulls `stateRef.current` whenever `editor` is null, and both handlers early-return on `!state` (:123, :132), so the replace can never run in the branch where `editor?.` short-circuits. The find bar is also the only production consumer of `FindReplaceState` (exported at packages/docs/src/index.ts:168; sole non-test import at docs-find-bar.tsx:4), so there is no second unguarded consumer. The finding's cited lines are additionally misread — :118 is a comment line and :126 is `syncHighlights()`. The trailing mentions of undoFn/redoFn and the table ops are inside editor.ts, not the "entry points outside editor.ts" this finding is framed around, and are not the site it names as needing to change.
